A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DC-CoT benchmark. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across revisions and relocations.

before.justification: v1 reports original student-model evaluations, teacher comparisons, data-volume experiments and out-of-distribution transfer results in Tables 1–5 and Figures 5–6.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds visual-model evaluations, a logit-distillation comparison, human judge validation, efficiency measurements and confidence intervals.

M1.justification: Section 4.3.2 introduces an uncertainty-based selection procedure that prioritizes examples with student entropy above 0.5 during zero-shot inference. The existing augmentation, reverse-thinking, filtering and mixing procedures remain. Added descriptions of prompt constraints and ground-truth conditioning do not establish changes to the previously evaluated procedures.

E1.justification: v2 adds actual CLEVR evaluations in Tables 1 and 6, extending visual reasoning coverage. OK-VQA already appeared in v1's setup and transfer experiments, so its additional results do not introduce a new dataset. Existing textual, agentic and OOD dataset coverage is retained.

E2.justification: The comparison scope expands beyond the original prompting and text-supervision baselines: Table 2 evaluates standard logit-based KD using KL divergence, while Table 6 compares uncertainty-based selection against the existing filters. Table 10 also introduces No-CoT comparisons for Mistral and Gemma on core reasoning tasks. These are evaluated comparators, not merely new citations.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include an ARC comparison using a Llama-3.1-70B teacher, visual experiments with Qwen-2.5-VL-8B and DeepSeek-VL2 students, human assessment of 100 sampled SQA/GSM8K instances, and throughput measurements on one A100-80GB GPU. Existing LoRA settings, training epochs, data-volume conditions and OOD pairings are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds a human-agreement analysis of automated filtering, tests whether the strategies extend to a mixture-of-experts student, and analyzes generation-token costs and inference efficiency in Appendix G. These address reliability, architectural generality and computational cost. The original student-size, data-volume, OOD and browser-example analyses remain, sometimes relocated.

E5.justification: v1 reports three-run textual averages without confidence intervals. Appendix H in v2 states that experiments use three seeds and first reports 95% confidence intervals for No CoT and Reverse CoT across three models and three tasks. It interprets interval separation as statistical significance, but does not specify the interval calculation or a formal testing procedure. An increase in run count is not established.

E6.justification: Matched entries in the original main result tables remain numerically unchanged. Substantial new results include ARC accuracies of 69.2% for Reverse, 64.8% for logit KD and 60.4% for vanilla CoT under the new 70B-teacher setting; DeepSeek-VL2 OK-VQA scores of 51.82% with teacher filtering versus 45.46% with vanilla CoT; additional visual results; judge agreement of 0.84; and efficiency measurements. These are added results, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: The mathematical treatment of data transformation, augmentation and filtering is substantively unchanged. Explanations of existing symbols and correction of source/target wording are clarifications. Neither version contains theoretical propositions or proofs, and the new empirical statistics introduce no formal derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the benchmark contribution and principal findings. The revised conclusion extends structured-logic recommendations to code, which is not experimentally evaluated, and strengthens modality-specific guidance by asserting that simpler heuristics fail to verify agentic and visual grounding. Much of the underlying task-specific advice already appeared in v1.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations about learning shared valid logic despite noisy augmented traces, the desirability of strict automated judging, reasoning supervision versus logit matching, and applicability to MoE students. Appendix G additionally argues that generation costs are incurred once without inference-time overhead. These extend the interpretation considerably, while the budget and hardware limitations in Appendix A remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 newly describes prompt constraints, ground-truth conditioning, the entropy cutoff and hardware/software for efficiency measurements. It replaces the anonymous code link with a named GitHub repository link and removes the direct dataset link. Existing training hyperparameters and dataset statistics remain unchanged; the new reproducibility statement promises seed information without listing specific seeds.

R1.justification: v2 adds the Johnson et al. CLEVR reference and explicitly distinguishes its reasoning-transfer augmentation from general Self-Instruct-style generation and its black-box approach from white-box KD. The main related-work discussion and previously cited works are otherwise retained. Conversion to author–year citations is a presentation change.

P1.justification: The narrative is substantially reorganized: task descriptions move from Section 3.2 to Appendix E, student-size analysis moves to Appendix F, and OOD settings move to Appendix C.3. The main model-analysis section gains an architecture/selection subsection, the conclusion is rewritten, and ethics, reproducibility and LLM-use statements are added. Much of the retained scientific prose remains similar.

P2.justification: v2 changes the document template and typography, introduces colored method headings and table groups, expands Table 1 with two visual columns, and adds five tables covering KD, visual architectures, costs, efficiency and confidence intervals. Existing figures are retained with limited diagram edits and relocation; the student-size plot moves to the appendix. This is a substantial display and layout revision.

improvement.justification: The direct KD comparison, judge-agreement check and confidence intervals address gaps in v1's comparative and statistical support, providing a modest net improvement. The benefit is limited by incomplete protocol documentation and new inconsistencies: Appendix G claims a 6–9× speedup where Table 9 supports about 1.6×, and Table 1 retains its old visual-plus-agentic averages after adding two visual columns. The added validation is useful, but its reporting needs correction.
